content: A piped link is a hyperlink within a project or to a sister project that is displayed with a label different from the actual name of the page it links to. This allows the integration of a word or phrase into the text of a page without requiring the exact wording to match the name of the linked page. For example, instead of using see also, a piped link can seamlessly connect relevant content. When using a compatible browser and depending on user preferences, the actual linked page can still be identified. Hovering over the link will display the name of the linked page in a tooltip or the status bar. The term piped refers to the use of the pipe character | to separate the displayed text from the actual link. For instance, a link like `[[How to set up a coffee house|coffee house setup]]` will display as coffee house setup while linking to the How to set up a coffee house page. This is particularly useful when the displayed text needs to be contextually relevant, such as using station in an article about trains to imply train station. This approach is more user-friendly than linking to a disambiguation page like station, which might require additional navigation. An alternative to piped links is using a redirect page. For example, creating a redirect page titled How to set up a coffee house that points to the desired content allows the link to be written as `[[How to set up a coffee house]]`. However, this method has some drawbacks. The tooltip that appears when hovering over the link will only show the displayed text, not the target page. Additionally, changes to the redirect page will appear in Related changes, and the redirect message on the target page may clutter the interface. Despite these limitations, redirects can be useful if they are already in place or serve multiple purposes. In some cases, the link title may need to convey additional information not present in the target page's name. For example, a page titled 48 cm could redirect to a page about the unit Foot (unit of length). This allows the link to provide specific context while still directing users to the appropriate content. The pipe trick is a feature that simplifies piped links. If the text after the | is left empty, the system automatically generates a shortened version of the page name. For example: `[[Help:Pipe|]]` becomes `[[Help:Pipe]]` and is displayed as Pipe. `[[Template:Example|]]` becomes `[[Template:Example]]` and is displayed as Example. `[[Boston, Massachusetts|]]` becomes `[[Boston, Massachusetts]]` and is displayed as Boston. The pipe trick removes namespace prefixes (e.g., Help:), text in parentheses at the end, or text after a comma if no parentheses are present. However, this feature has limitations. It may not work for interlanguage links or links with a starting colon, and in some projects, piped links may not render as hyperlinks at all. For external links, a space is used instead of the pipe character. For example, `[http://example.com Example]` creates a link to http://example.com with the displayed text Example. Both piped links and external links are sometimes referred to as clean links due to their streamlined appearance.
